hook: Yejin Choi is a computer scientist known for advancing commonsense reasoning and evaluation methods in natural language processing. She earned a bachelor's degree in computer engineering from Seoul National University and a PhD in computer science from Cornell University, then built her academic career at the University of Washington, where she held the Brett Helsel Career Development Professorship from 2020 to 2023 and the Wissner-Slivka Chair from 2023 to 2024. Her research has focused on giving machines the kind of everyday, common sense knowledge that humans take for granted, and on building benchmarks that reveal when large language models fail at reasoning tasks that seem simple to people. In 2022 she was named a MacArthur Fellow for this work and became an ACL Fellow the same year. She has since moved to Stanford University, where she holds the Dieter Schwarz Foundation Professorship in Computer Science and is a Senior Fellow at the Stanford Institute for Human-Centered AI, continuing work on democratizing generative AI through smaller models and on pluralistic alignment of AI systems with diverse human values.

quick_facts: Earned a PhD in computer science from Cornell University and a BS in computer engineering from Seoul National University
Held the Brett Helsel Career Development Professorship (2020 to 2023) and the Wissner-Slivka Chair (2023 to 2024) at the University of Washington
Named a MacArthur Fellow in 2022 for work on commonsense reasoning in AI
Named an ACL Fellow in 2022 and has received multiple best and outstanding paper awards at NeurIPS, ACL and EMNLP
Now the Dieter Schwarz Foundation Professor of Computer Science and a Senior Fellow at Stanford HAI
Research focuses on democratizing generative AI with smaller, more efficient models and on pluralistic alignment of AI with diverse human values
